title: Acids, Bases and pH
seo_title: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Acids, Bases and pH Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Acids and bases; pH value; reactions of acids
standard_text: The pH scale; indicators; reactions of acids with bases (neutralisation), metal oxides, metal carbonates and metals, forming salts, water, carbon dioxide and hydrogen; uses of neutralisation. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Matter and Materials: Acids and bases; pH value; reactions of acids)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the pH scale, indicators, neutralisation, and reactions of acids with metal oxides, carbonates and metals. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
body_html:
How to think about it

The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic. Universal indicator shows the pH by its colour.

Acids react with: bases (acid + base → salt + water: neutralisation), metal oxides (acid + metal oxide → salt + water), metal carbonates (acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide) and some metals (acid + metal → salt + hydrogen). Hydrochloric acid makes chlorides; sulfuric acid makes sulfates.

Example

What gas forms when an acid reacts with a carbonate?

It turns limewater milky.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Which salt forms from hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide?

Hydrochloric acid makes chlorides.

Answer: sodium chloride

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a salt is always table salt.
  • Thinking pH 4 is more basic than pH 6.
  • Forgetting the water in neutralisation.

items.q: Which test identifies iodide ions?
c: acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous silver nitrate (white precipitate)
add dilute acid (effervescence; the gas (carbon dioxide) turns limewater milky)
acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous barium nitrate (white precipitate)
acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous silver nitrate (yellow precipitate)
items.e: iodide, I⁻: acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous silver nitrate.

items.q: A solution contains nitrate ions. The test is to add aqueous sodium hydroxide, then aluminium foil, and warm carefully. What is the positive result?
c: effervescence; the gas (carbon dioxide) turns limewater milky
ammonia gas is given off, turning damp red litmus blue
items.e: nitrate, NO₃⁻: add aqueous sodium hydroxide, then aluminium foil, and warm carefully → ammonia gas is given off, turning damp red litmus blue.

items.q: A solution is tested: add aqueous sodium hydroxide, then aluminium foil, and warm carefully. Result: ammonia gas is given off, turning damp red litmus blue. Which anion is present?
items.e: This is the test for nitrate, NO₃⁻.

add aqueous sodium hydroxide, then aluminium foil, and warm carefully (ammonia gas is given off, turning damp red litmus blue)
items.e: carbonate, CO₃²⁻: add dilute acid.
